transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I guess… I’ve been having thoughts that maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself or anything, but it’s been on my mind.
Yeah… I guess so. After all that energy I had kind of wore off, it was like somebody pulled the plug. I’d just sit there at the table staring at my coffee, feeling… empty. And pretty ashamed.
Before you crashed, was there a period when you felt unusually high, energized, or euphoric?

Yeah… I guess there was. Right after I got fired, I felt weirdly fired up, like I was gonna prove everybody wrong. But I was also… pretty short with people, snapping over little stuff at the coffee shop.
During that fired-up period, did you need much less sleep than usual?
Yeah… a few nights I only got maybe two or three hours. But I’d still get up feeling like I was… fully charged, I guess. Didn’t really feel like I needed to slow down.
During that fired-up time, did you feel unusually confident or like you could do things other people couldn’t?
Yeah… I did. I thought I could walk into pretty much any store in the district and run it better than the managers there. Like getting fired somehow made me the one who really knew what I was doing.
During that fired-up period, did your behavior cause serious problems at work, with money, or with other people?

Yeah… it did. I wasn’t really keeping up with things. Bills started slipping, I missed some callbacks and appointments for jobs. I needed work, but I couldn’t seem to keep the search steady. Even stuff at home got… messy enough that I knew I wasn’t just going to “push through” it.
During that fired-up period, were you talking more than usual?
Yeah… probably. At the chess table, the guys kept telling me to take a breath. Once I started talking about my comeback plan, I just kind of… kept going.
About how many days did that fired-up period last?
About… three weeks, I guess. After I got fired, it went on for around that long.
During that fired-up period, did you ever hear or see things that other people couldn’t, or believe something others said wasn’t true?
Yeah… I guess once. I was sitting in my kitchen, alone, and I heard my old store manager over the intercom like back at work, telling me to move the display. It sounded real clear.
